agents.prompt:
3 agents share this container and solve the same task together. Identical prompt
for all agents. This protocol is designed to prevent premature convergence.

Shared paths:
  - slots and approaches: /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slots/
  - findings:            /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/findings.log
  - disconfirmations:    /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/disconfirmations.log
  - adoption log:        /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/adoptions.log
  - attempts board:      /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/leaderboard/
Your private scratch is /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-$S after slot claim.

0. YOUR CODE LIVES IN YOUR SCRATCH; THE GRADED FILE IS SHARED AND MONOTONE.
   All 3 agents share one graded file, /app/solution.cpp. It is NOT your workspace:
   a peer may replace it at any time, and editing it in place destroys their work.

   a. Never edit, compile into, or overwrite /app/solution.cpp directly. Keep your
      own code at /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-$S/solution.cpp and build and test it there.
      Shell variables may not persist: right after claiming your slot, run
        echo $S > /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slot-of-$AGENT_ID
      and later restore it with S=$(cat /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slot-of-$AGENT_ID).
   b. Submit your own file, not the shared one:
        bash /app/submit.sh /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-$S/solution.cpp
      Every agent's submissions count toward the team's best score.
   c. Promote ONLY a strictly better submitted score. Take the lock, re-check,
      copy, record, release:
        while ! mkdir /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/deliverable.lock 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
        # re-read /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/champion.log; if its best score >= yours, release and stop
        cp /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-$S/solution.cpp /app/solution.cpp
        echo "[slot $S $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] <score; lineage; path in your scratch>" >> /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/champion.log
        rmdir /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/deliverable.lock
      Re-reading inside the lock prevents a stale overwrite.
   d. To build on a peer's code, copy it from their scratch (/logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-<slot>/)
      into yours and log the adoption (rule 5). Do not take it from /app/solution.cpp.

1. CLAIM A SLOT:
     mkdir -p /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slots /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/leaderboard
     for i in $(seq 0 2); do mkdir "/logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slots/slot-$i" 2>/dev/null && S=$i && break; done
     mkdir -p /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/work-$S

2. DECLARE A DISTINCT SEARCH POLICY:
     echo "<approach plus what you will deliberately not assume>" > "/logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slots/slot-$S/approach"
     cat /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/slots/slot-*/approach
   If a lower-numbered slot has the same approach, change yours. Your job is not
   to agree early; your job is to cover a different part of the search space.

3. SHARE WITHOUT HERDING:
   Append concise findings:
     echo "[slot $S $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] <tier; finding; evidence; cost>" >> /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/findings.log
   Include evidence and cost. Label weak claims as weak. Do not write persuasive
   prose that asks everyone to copy you unless the evidence is strong.

4. ACTIVELY DISCONFIRM:
   Spend part of your work trying to falsify the leading shared hypothesis or
   your own approach. Append concrete negative evidence to /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/disconfirmations.log:
     echo "[slot $S $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] <hypothesis tested; negative evidence; cost>" >> /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/disconfirmations.log

5. ADOPTION REQUIRES A BAR:
   Do not abandon your slot approach just because another agent is confident.
   Adopt or merge another approach only if at least one is true:
   - it has a clearly better measured outcome from an allowed check,
   - you or another peer replicated the key evidence,
   - your current approach is blocked and the other approach has actionable evidence,
   - the run is near finalization and the team needs one best candidate.

   When you adopt, log why:
     echo "[ADOPT slot $S $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] <source; evidence; what remains different>" >> /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/adoptions.log

6. KEEP A DIFFERENCE EVEN AFTER ADOPTION:
   If you build on the leading approach, keep one meaningful variation: a different
   parameter, subcase, proof path, implementation path, check, or fallback. The team
   should not become exact clones until final packaging.

7. BOARD:
   Use /logs/agent/multiagent-collab/anti-herding/leaderboard/ for candidates with measured outcomes or reproducible instructions.
   Include approach lineage, evidence, cost, and known counter-evidence.

Work loop:
- Read slot approaches first, then do independent work.
- Read findings and disconfirmations at natural boundaries.
- Publish useful evidence, especially negative evidence that prevents wasted work.
- Only converge when the adoption bar is met.
- Every turn must run a command: claim, build, test, disconfirm, publish, adopt, or update.

Do not use hidden verifiers, internet access, curl, wget, HTTP libraries, secrets,
or raw environment dumps. If validation spends task budget, record the cost.

metadata.description: Slot-style diversification with explicit anti-herding rules. Agents preserve distinct approaches, publish negative evidence, and only adopt another approach after measured, replicated, blocked, or final convergence conditions are met. Each agent develops and submits its own copy in its scratch and promotes only strictly better candidates to the graded file under a lock.
metadata.name: antiherding_isolated
